SHEET 01 / 03

Engineering Projects

SENIOR CAPSTONE

Personal Lunar Transporter — Thermal Protection System

TEAM LEAD, 6-PERSON TEAM
AUG 2023 – MAY 2024
PARTNERTrek Bicycles
PROTECTION MEDIUMParaffin wax, phase-change
ASSUMED MELT MARGIN~6°C below min. op. temp
OBSERVED MARGIN2–3°C
CORE TEMP SENSINGThermocouple through axle
LOAD METHODChain/sprocket + bicycle
LOAD MEASUREMENTBreaker bar + torque sensor
  • Led a six-person team through the full project lifecycle — scheduling, task allocation, technical reviews — coordinating with Trek Bicycles and a second engineering team on cross-system integration.
  • No test apparatus existed for this system, so I designed and fabricated one from scratch: a sealed, rated insulation box to simulate the lunar thermal environment, a custom stand to hold the free-spinning hub motor, and a load path running from a sprocket on the rotating assembly, through a chain, to a repurposed bicycle — with a breaker bar and torque sensor in line to control and measure the applied load.
  • Drilled through the fabricated axle to seat a thermocouple at the motor's core for an accurate internal reading, with a second thermocouple in the insulation box tracking ambient environment separately.
  • Testing showed the wax's real melt margin was 2–3°C, tighter than the ~6°C assumed from its rated spec. The system passed, but I flagged the gap between assumption and reality and recommended sourcing or formulating a lower-melting-point wax in future iterations to build in real safety margin.
SHEET 02 / 03

Multi-Stage Gearbox

ME 305 MACHINE DESIGN LAB — WITH GAVIN BOTTS & ISSA MEBOE

Multi-Stage Gearbox

3-PERSON TEAM
AUG 2023 – DEC 2023
RATED LOAD50 lb
MOTOR INPUT0.15 hp @ 3785 rpm
OUTPUT TORQUE2.49 ft·lb (req. 1.56)
DESIGN LIFE10⁸ cycles
MIN. GEAR FoS (BEND/CONTACT)30.97 / 3.62
MIN. SHAFT FoS3.78 (Shaft B)
HOUSING6061-Al, 6×6×4 in
EST. COST$331.31 (budget $400)
  • Designed a four-gear, three-shaft gearbox to convert a 0.15 hp, 3785 rpm motor input into enough torque to lift a 50-lb load over a required life of 10⁸ cycles, performing full AGMA bending and contact stress analysis on all four gears and DE-Goodman fatigue sizing on all three shafts by hand.
  • Every gear cleared bending and contact factors of safety well above 1.0 (minimum 30.97 bending, 3.62 contact); the critical shaft (Shaft B, ½" diameter) still carried a factor of safety of 3.78 under combined bending and torsional loading.
  • Modeled the full gear train and a 6×6×4 in 6061-aluminum housing in SOLIDWORKS with GD&T — well under the project's 12×15×4 in size cap — sourcing gears, shafts, and bearings from McMaster-Carr and machining the housing and end caps in-house on the CNC lathe and waterjet.
  • Delivered a design that exceeded the required output torque (2.49 ft·lb vs. 1.56 ft·lb needed) at an estimated cost of $331.31, under the project's $400 budget.

PERSONAL SOLIDWORKS PROJECT

Variable-Area Exhaust Nozzle

SELF-DIRECTED
SEP 2026 – PRESENT
PETAL COUNT12 primary / 12 secondary
ACTUATIONDual-servo, guided axial ring
VALIDATED STROKE3.85 mm
ROTATION RANGE0° – 15.5°, interference-free
STATUSCAD complete · drawings next
  • Designing a 12-primary/12-secondary-petal variable-area exhaust-nozzle mechanism in SolidWorks on my own initiative — a guided axial actuation ring, synchronized linkages, and a dual-servo actuation concept.
  • Iteratively redesigned the primary petal hinge/crank geometry to reduce mechanism packaging while preserving actuation kinematics; validated a 3.85 mm actuator stroke with interference-free operation from 0° to 15.5° petal rotation.
  • Next planned steps: production drawings with GD&T, followed by 3D printing and personal assembly to test fit, kinematics, and servo actuation.
